Now the seventh Maṇḍala begins.

In this regard, "Agniḥ naraḥ" is the first hymn (*sūkta*), consisting of twenty-five verses. Here is the index (*anukramaṇikā*): "For Agni, there are five [verses] in excess; the first eighteen are *virāj*s.
Since it has been stated that "Vasiṣṭha saw the seventh maṇḍala," the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Vasiṣṭha, the seer of the maṇḍala.
The first eighteen verses are *virāj* meters consisting of eleven syllables each; the remaining verses are *triṣṭubh* according to the rule regarding unspecified meters.
According to the rule concerning the *maṇḍala* and so forth, Agni is the deity.
This hymn is the *ājya* recitation for the *Viśvajit* sacrifice.
It is stated in the Sūtra: "For the *Viśvajit*, 'O men, Agni... is the *ājya*" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 8.7).
Here, in the fourth day of the four-night rite known as the *iṣutūrvi*, this very hymn serves as the *ājya* recitation.
For it is stated: "The hymn 'Agni naraḥ' is used on the fourth day" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 10.2).
In the ten-night sacrificial session (*daśarātra*), this hymn is the *jātavedasya* insertion (*nivid-vāna*) on the fourth day.
And it is prescribed in the Sūtra: "'Agni naraḥ' is the hymn for the Āgnimāruta [laud]" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 8.8).
In the Mahāvrata, there is the Ājya-śastra for the Agnidh. Likewise, it is enjoined in the fifth Āraṇyaka: "The Ājya and Prauga [belong] to the Viśvajit" (Ai. Ā. 5.1.1).

On the Avivākya day, during the Prātaranuvāka, the first triplet of Anuṣṭubh verses beginning with "tvam agne vasūnām" (O Agni, you of the Vasus... is to be inserted in place of the [standard] Anuṣṭubhs.

For it is prescribed: "On the tenth day, in the place of the *anuṣṭubh* verses, [one recites] the triplet beginning with 'Agni naro dīdhitibhiraraṇyoḥ' in the sacrifice dedicated to Agni" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 8.12).
The first six verses of that [triplet] serve as the *stotriya* and *anurūpa* in the *āgnimāruta* litany on that very day.
And it is stated in the *Sūtra*: "'Agni naro dīdhitibhiraraṇyoḥ' are the *stotriya* and *anurūpa*" (*Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra* 8.12).
This same [procedure] applies even in the case of the homa in the maṇḍala and so forth.
At the third iṣṭi of the Ādhāna, "Preddhaḥ" is the invitatory verse (anuvākyā) for the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "The two verses 'Preddho agne' and 'Imo agne' are the two saṃyājyās" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 2.1).
Similarly, in other cases such as the *dīkṣaṇīyā* and others, there is an invitatory verse (*anuvākyā*) for the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering.
In the *prāyaṇīyā* sacrifice, there are two verses for the *yājyā* and *anuvākyā* of the *sviṣṭakṛt*, beginning with "sedabhiragnīn.
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "'sedabhiragnīrtyasvantyāniti dve saṃyājye' (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.3)."
In the third offering of the Āghāra sacrifice, "imo agne" is the invitatory verse (*yājyā*) for the Sviṣṭakṛt oblation.
As it is stated in the Sūtra: "The two *saṃyājyās* are 'imo agne'... (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 2.1).
Likewise, in other instances such as the Dīkṣaṇīyā and others, this is the Sviṣṭakṛt *yājyā*.
In the Prātaranuvāka, within the Āgneya kratu, in the Triṣṭubh metre, and in the Āśvina Śastra, there are five verses beginning with "tvam agne suhavaḥ.
This is also stated in the Sūtra: "tvam agne suhavo raṇvasaṃdak" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 4.13).
With their prayers and with the movement of their hands, the men have generated from the two fire-sticks the praiseworthy Agni—
the far-seeing lord of the house and the active one.
Men, producing with their prayers the praiseworthy, far-seeing, and active lord of the house from the two fire-sticks by the movement of their hands—[they produce] Agni. 1.

Men—the leaders and officiating priests—produced from the two kindling woods Agni, who is present there, by means of the movement of their hands—that is, by the motion of their hands—and with their fingers, which are called *dīdhitayaḥ* because they are employed in ritual acts. [They produced him] who is praised, highly extolled, visible from afar, or seeing from afar, the lord of the house, the protector of homes, the active one, or the one who has come and extended himself. Or rather, Agni was born from the friction of the two kindling woods.
"By the falling from the hand, through the dropping from the hand, they produce one who is praised, far-sighted, a master of the house, and wise" (Nirukta 5.10).

The Vasus have established that Agni within the dwelling, for protection from every quarter—he who is beautiful to behold, worthy of honor, and who has been ever-present in the home as one to be served with offerings. That Agni, who is worthy of worship (*dakṣāyya*) in the house, who is eternal (*nitya*), him—the one beautiful to behold—the Vasus, those who provide dwellings and are most excellent, have established within the dwelling for protection from any source whatsoever.

To him, the skillful one, comes the youthful woman at evening with garments, bearing oblations and dripping with ghee; to him also comes his own Aramati, seeking wealth. O Agni, may your face—your brilliance—be visible to us. May the mortals who are the descendants of the seers (ārṣeyas) or those who are the leaders of men (naraḥ), the sacrificers who have distributed [the offerings] in many places, establish it for themselves;
even as it is for them, so for us, being well-disposed and gracious-minded through these praises or hymns, be present here at this sacrifice.
May these heroes, men in the slaying of Vṛtra, overcome all godless illusions—those who further my praiseworthy prayer. 10.
May these men, heroes in the slaying of Vṛtra, overcome all godless illusions—those who restore my praiseworthy prayer. 10.

Those men who praise—that is, extol or speak of—my excellent and sublime *dhi* (work or hymn), these affectionate men are heroes for me in the slaying of Vṛtra, in battles; let them overcome all the godless, demonic illusions.
24 O Agni, let us not sit in the void among men, nor around you in the state of being headless or lacking heroes. O Dweller in the House, dwell in houses that abound with progeny. 11.
O Agni, let us not sit in an empty dwelling among men; let there be no lack of offspring, nor herolessness around you, O House-Lord, in dwellings filled with progeny. 11.

O Agni, may we not dwell—that is, may we not reside—in a house that is empty, meaning devoid of sons and others; nor may we settle in the houses of other men. O Agni, who art beneficial to the dwellings, [may we not be] "aśeṣasaḥ," that is, childless.

Because "toka" and "śeṣas" are listed among the names for sons, [the meaning is as follows]: being joined with "avīratā," that is, lacking heroic sons, yet serving you, we dwell in houses and dwellings filled with progeny.
May the glory of Yama ever approach our sacrifice, our home which is rich in offspring and noble descendants, increasing through its own birth and progeny. 12.
May Fortune ever attend our sacrifice, which is rich in progeny and blessed with good offspring—a dwelling that increases through its own birth and through its descendants. 12.

O Agni, grant to us that dwelling—a home rich in progeny, accompanied by servants and the like, endowed with noble offspring, and flourishing through our own legitimate sons—grant it to us, O Agni; this is the ellipsis.

Protect us, O Agni, from the rākṣasa with your bright [flames]; protect us from the sinner who seeks to harm us with your shaking [flames]. With you as my ally, may I overcome those who attack in battle. 13.
Protect us! O Agni, protect us from the *rakṣas* that is reddish-brown; protect us from the dark, malevolent one. With you as our ally, may we overcome those who attack in battle. 13.
O Agni, protect us from the *vraja*—from the hostile, immortal realm of the *rakṣas*, the demon—and guard us!
Furthermore, protect us from the *varuṣa*, the non-giver, the *aghāyu*, the one who desires evil, and from the *dhūti*, the injurer.
Moreover, with you as my ally (*yuja*) and companion, may I overcome those who seek to extend their power over us (*pratanāyūn*).

May this Agni indeed surpass all others, where the vigorous son, firm-handed, with a thousand paths, meets with the imperishable syllable. 14. May he, this Agni, indeed surpass all others, where the vigorous son, firm-handed, with a thousand paths, meets with the imperishable syllable. 14.
May he, our own Vabhi—the Āhavanīya fire and so forth—triumph over the other Vamris belonging to others; may he surpass them.
In this [fire], let there be one who is *vājī*—possessing food or strength—and *vīḷupāṇi*, firm-handed;
for "vīḷu" and "cyautna" are among the names for strength.

O Agni, being masters of wealth, may we, offering the eternal oblations to you, pour forth many invocations and sacrificial offerings in the sacrifice, performing both modes of conveyance—the hymn and the litany. O Agni, being masters of wealth, may we, offering the eternal oblations such as the *agnihotra* and others to you, and performing both modes of conveyance—the hymn (*stotra*) and the litany (*śastra*)—pour forth many invocations and sacrificial offerings (*āhavanāni*) in the sacrifice (*miyedha*).

O Agni, you who are eternal, carry these most desirable oblations toward the assembly of the gods; let them accept our fragrant offerings. O Agni, being eternal and unceasing, carry these most desirable oblations—these offerings most exceedingly pleasing—to the assembly of the gods (*devatātām*). Go toward them! And let the gods individually accept and desire these fragrant, beautiful offerings of ours.

O Agni, do not deliver us to childlessness; do not deliver us to ill-clad poverty, nor to this lack of wisdom. Do not deliver us to hunger, nor to the demon, O upholder of Truth (*ṛtāvan*). Do not lead us astray in our home, nor in the forest. O Agni, do not abandon us to childlessness (*avīrata*); do not abandon us to ill-clad poverty (*durvāsas*); do not abandon us to this lack of wisdom (*amatī*), which strikes us down. Do not abandon us to hunger (*kṣudh*); do not abandon us to the powerful demon (*rakṣas*). O *ṛtāvan*, you who possess Truth, do not lead us astray (*juhurthāḥ*)—do not harm us—in our home (*dame*), nor in the forest (*vane*). (The root *hurch* means "to be crooked" or "to deceive. Do not lead us astray in the forest either.

Now, O Agni, do thou instruct my prayers; O God, bestow [wealth] upon the liberal patrons. May we both [patrons and singers] partake in thy bounty. Do you all protect us ever with blessings. (20) Now, O Agni, do thou instruct my prayers; O God, bestow [wealth] upon the liberal patrons. May we both [patrons and singers] partake in thy bounty. Do you all protect us ever with blessings. (20) O Agni, for me—on my behalf—instruct quickly (nu) my prayers (*brahmāṇi*), that is, make them excellently purified. Furthermore, O shining God, pour forth food for us, the liberal patrons (*maghavadbhyaḥ*) who possess oblations. In thy bounty (*rātau*), may we—the singers and the reciters, or alternatively, those who praise and the sacrificers—both [partake] in it. Do you all protect us ever with blessings. (20)

1. *kha-gha-jha-ta-bha-āhuvāma*; *na-ājuhavāma*; *śa-juhuvāma*. 2. *jha-śa-ṛtavaḥ*. 3. *ta-ya-ubhayāsaḥ* means "both" (*ubhaye*). 4. *jha-yatha vā*; *ta-na-bha-ya-śa-yathā vā*. *v-syāma* means "may we be exceedingly. *v-naḥ* means "us," [referring to] we and all those surrounding you. *v-svastibhiḥ* means "by means of indestructible auspicious blessings."
And thus Yāska says: "Svasti signifies non-destruction; āsti is a form of praise; svasti [is a benediction]" (Nirukta 3.21).
O you who are ever-present, protect us!

O Agni, you who are easy to invoke, delightful in appearance, shine with beautiful luster, O Son of Strength! Let not our own son, born of us, be ever consumed by smoke while dwelling with you; let not the heroic man, our kinsman, be lost to us. 21. tvam agne suhavo raṇvasandak sudītī sūno sahaso dīdihi | mā tve sacā tanaye nitye ā dhṛk mā vīro asmabhyo naryo vidāsīt ||21|| O Agni, you who are easy to invoke, delightful in appearance, shine with beautiful luster, O Son of Strength! Let not our own son, born of us, be ever consumed by smoke while dwelling with you; let not the heroic man, our kinsman, be lost to us. 21.

O Agni, son of strength, born of power, easy to invoke and well-invoked, you who are pleasant to behold—do you, O Agni, knowing the great prosperity, bring us from the patrons that vast wealth with beautiful radiance, by which we, O powerful one, may rejoice with undiminished life and heroic sons. 24. O Agni, knowing our great prosperity, bring vast wealth to the patrons, by which we, O powerful one, may rejoice with undiminished life and heroic sons. 24.
O Agni, you who are the knower of our great *suvita*— that is, the auspicious deed; meaning,
knowing our auspicious action— you,
bring hither abundant and great wealth (*rayi*) for us, your liberal patrons (*suribhyaḥ*) and worshippers.
He specifies wealth itself:

O powerful and mighty Agni, by that wealth through which we, your praisers, may be undecaying—unwasted in our lifespan—and being possessed of good heroes, with noble sons and grandsons, may we rejoice and exult in the assembly.

Now, O Agni, do thou instruct my prayers; O God, grant them a good dwelling for the sake of the liberal patrons. May we both be recipients of thy bounty. Do you all protect us always with blessings. 25. Now, my, prayers, O Agni, do thou instruct upward; thou, O God, [grant] good dwellings for the liberal patrons. In the giving, may we be [recipients], both of us. From thee, do you [gods] protect us with blessings always. 25.
This ṛc has already been explained previously.
By illuminating the meaning of the Vedas and dispelling the darkness of the heart,
may Vidyātīrthamaheśvara bestow the four aims of human existence.

Thus ends the first chapter of the fifth book (*aṣṭaka*) in the *Ṛgveda-saṃhitā-bhāṣya*, titled *Vedārthaprakāśa*, composed by Sāyaṇācārya, the bearer of the burden of the empire of the illustrious King Vīrabukka—the glorious sovereign over kings, supreme lord, and promoter of the Vedic path—under the patronage of Mādhava.

**Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.** I bow to that Great Lord Vidyātīrtha, whose breath is the Vedas, and who created the entire universe from the Vedas. The second hymn, consisting of eleven verses beginning with "juṣasva naḥ," is the *ārṣa* of Vasiṣṭha and is composed in the *triṣṭubh* meter. Because the first word is mentioned [in the index], it is designated as the *āprī* hymn dedicated to Tanūnapāt. The specific deities for each verse, beginning with Samidh, have been stated. Thus it is enumerated: "The eleven beginning with juṣasva are the *āprīs*. This is the *āprī* hymn for the animal sacrifice (*paśu-iṣṭi*). It is prescribed in the Sūtra: "For the Vasiṣṭhas, [the verse] 'juṣasva naḥ samidham'" (Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra 3.2). Furthermore, it was previously stated that this is the invitatory verse (*anu-vākyā*) for the cake-offering (*puroḍāśa*) in the sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ during the Patnīsaṃyāja, as well as in the animal sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ. **Verse 1:** juṣasva naḥ samidhamadya śocā bṛhadyajataṃ dhūmamṛṇvan | upa spṛśa divyaṃ sānu stūpaiḥ saṃ raśmibhistatanuḥ sūryasya || 1 || O Agni, enjoy our fuel today; shine forth mightily, emitting the sacred smoke. Touch the celestial ridge with your flames; extend yourself together with the rays of the Sun. **Word-for-word:** *juṣasva* (enjoy), *naḥ* (our), *samidham* (fuel), *adya* (today), *agne* (O Agni), *śoca* (shine), *bṛhat* (greatly), *yajatam* (sacred), *dhūmam* (smoke), *ṛṇvan* (emitting), *upa* (towards), *spṛśa* (touch), *divyam* (celestial), *sānu* (ridge/summit), *stūpaiḥ* (with flames), *sam* (together), *raśmibhiḥ* (with rays), *tatanuḥ* (extend), *sūryasya* (of the Sun).
1. One who knows the letters *kha*, *kṣa*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, *ya*, *śa*.
2. O Agni, born of the sacrificial act (*śakarmaja*), enjoy (*juṣasva*) and accept (*sevasva*) our fuel-stick (*samidham*) today (*adya*).
O you who are worthy of sacrifice and praised, emitting the smoke, blaze forth intensely and shine!
Furthermore, touch the divine, elevated ridge of the atmosphere with your heated rays.
Moreover, unite yourself with the rays—that is, the splendors—of the sun.
We shall praise with sacrifices the greatness of these, of the one praised by men, the worshipful one;
those gods who are doers of good, pure, and bestowers of insight, enjoy both kinds of oblations.

We shall praise with sacrifices the greatness of these, of the one praised by men (Narāśaṃsa), the worshipful one—those gods who are doers of good deeds, pure, and bestowers of wisdom, who relish both kinds of oblations. 2.

O gods, who are well-performing, possessed of good wisdom or good deeds, pure and radiant, and sustainers of ritual acts (*dhiyaṃdhāḥ*), who enjoy—make palatable and consume—the two kinds of offerings, both those pertaining to the Soma sacrifice and those beginning with the *havissaṃsthā* rites; among them, we shall praise the greatness, the majesty, of the worshipful *Narāśaṃsa*, who is to be extolled by men, through sacrifices, oblations, or hymns. We praise him.
And thus Yāska says: "Men, sitting within it, praise;
'ami' is [the name of] Śākapūṇi, for he is praised by men.
Of him there is this [verse]."

"We shall praise with sacrifices the greatness of these [gods], of the one praised by men, the worshipful one—those who are performers of good deeds, pure, and sustainers of the prayer; may the gods make both kinds of oblations palatable: Soma and the others" (Nirukta 8.6).

We shall magnify for our sacrifice this Agni, who is worthy of praise, the Asura, the highly skillful, the messenger between the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) whose speech is true; like Manu, we celebrate him who was kindled by Manu from of old.

We shall ever exalt for our sacrifice Agni—the one to be praised, the Asura, the very skillful, the messenger between the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) whose word is true, kindled by Manu like Manu himself. 3.

O Adhvaryus, you [should] always fully honor for the sake of the sacrifice Agni—who is worthy of praise, the powerful one, the very wise one, who moves between the two worlds as the messenger of the gods carrying the oblation, whose speech is truth, and who was kindled by Manu like humans do now; that fire which was formerly kindled by Manu Prajāpati—[you should] always fully honor him.
The second person [of the verb] is changed into the first person by way of transposition.
Worshipful, bringing [offerings] with bent knees, they spread out the sacred grass (*barhis*) with reverence.
Invoking [the gods], cleanse the speckled, ghee-backed steed with the oblation.

Reverent, bearing [the oblation], they spread the sacred grass (barhis) upon their knees with homage. The cow, being invoked, [yields] the butter-backed [oblation]; O Adhvaryus, you who have spotted horses, purify [the sacrifice] with the oblation. 4.
1. [The sections] jha, śa, and tanvaḥ; [the sections] ta and tvadāyaiḥ; [the section] na and tattaiḥ do not exist. 2.
[The sections] kha, raumikāni, and the others; gha, the others, and the saumikāni; jha, ta, na, bha, and śa, and the saumikāni.
3. The ta-stoma belongs to the sacrifice.
4. Those who have performed good deeds and are doers of merit; 5. [The letters] kha, jha, ta, na, bha, śa are not present, as they are not found in human beings.

Seeking protection, approaching with knees bent, and bearing [the offering], they present the *barhis* grass along with the oblation and reverence to Agni. This very point is clarified: O Adhvaryus, you who offer the oblation, purify yourselves and attend upon Agni—the one whose back is sprinkled with ghee (*ghṛtapṛṣṭha*), the *barhis* which is joined with large drops of fat (*pṛṣaddhat*)—together with the sacrificial food. (5) The wise ones, desiring the gods, have opened wide the doors for the sake of the sacrifice, seeking chariots. Like two mothers licking their young, they have anointed them together at the gatherings, like flowing rivers. The wise ones, performing good deeds, desiring the gods, and seeking chariots, have opened wide the doors of the sacrificial hall for the sake of the divine service. Furthermore, at the sacrifices, like two mothers licking their calf, they have anointed the two ancient, eastward-pointed ladles (*juhū* and *upabhṛt*) with clarified butter, just as rivers anoint the fields with water. (6) And may the two celestial maidens, Dawn and Night, our great ones, like a cow easy to milk, sit upon the *barhis* grass, invoked by many, wealthy, worthy of sacrifice, and lead us toward prosperity. And may the two celestial maidens, Dawn and Night—those two youthful women, born in heaven, great, seated upon the *barhis*, invoked by many, wealthy, and worthy of sacrifice—like a cow easy to milk, sit down for our well-being. (7) O sages, among human sacrifices, I honor you two, the doers of deeds, the possessors of all-knowing wealth (*jātavedas*), so that I may worship. Make our sacrifice upright during the invocations; as such, you two win desirable treasures from among the gods. O divine Hotṛ-priests, sages, possessors of all-knowing wealth, performers of rites among human sacrifices—I honor you two so that I may worship. Moreover, during the invocations and hymns, make our straight sacrifice directed upward toward the gods; and as such, you two obtain desirable riches from among the gods, bestowing them upon us. 1. kha-ta-bha-rathakāmaśca; śa-rathamātmana icchataśca | 2. kha-bha-miśrarūpe | 3. kha-kṣa-ta-na-bha-śa- ‘divye...mahatyau’ is not present.

May Bhāratī with the Bhāratīs, Iḷā with the divine and human beings, Agni, and Sarasvatī with the Sārasvatas—may these three goddesses come hither and sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*). Although this group of four verses has already been explained in the eighth chapter of the second book of the *Ṛgveda Saṃhitā* (3.4.8–11), it is nevertheless briefly explained here as well due to the intervening distance. *Bhāratī*, the wife of Bharata (the Āditya), accompanied by the *Bhāratīs* and being well-disposed (*sajoṣāḥ*), may *Iḷā* together with the *daivaiḥ* (divine beings) and *manuṣyebhiḥ* (human beings born in the world of men) and *agniḥ* (Agni) come hither. May *Sarasvatī* together with the *sārasvatebhiḥ* (the Sārasvatas, the deities of the middle region) come toward us (*arvāk*). Having arrived, may the three goddesses sit down upon this *barhiḥ* (sacrificial grass). (Note: The second case ending is used in the sense of the first.)

O God Tvaṣṭṛ, being delighted, release for us that seed which is swift and nourishing; from which a hero is born—one who is skillful in action, very capable, a preparer of the pressing-stones, and a lover of the gods. O radiant God Tvaṣṭṛ, you who are rejoicing, release—that is, cause to flow forth—that seed of ours which is swift and nourishing. From that seed, a hero is born: one who is effective in ritual acts, highly dexterous, a master of the pressing-stones, and devoted to the gods.

O Lord of the Forest, release [the oblation] toward the gods; Agni, acting as the preparer (*śamitṛ*), prepares the offering. He alone, the most truthful Hotṛ, shall sacrifice, for he knows the generations of the gods. (10) O Lord of the Forest, release [the offering] toward the gods. Now follows an indirect praise: Agni, the Lord of the Forest, being the preparer (*śamitṛ*) in the form of the *śāmitra*, prepares—that is, impels—the offering. He alone, that very Lord of the Forest, being the most truthful invoker (*hotṛ*) of the gods, shall sacrifice; he shall perform the sacrifice just as he himself knows the births and origins of the gods.

Come hither, O Agni, being well-kindled, toward us, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods! Let Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacred grass. Svāhā! May the immortal gods rejoice! 11. Come hither, O Agni, being well-kindled, toward us, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods! Let Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacred grass. Svāhā! May the immortal gods rejoice! 11.
1. *kha-na-bha-śa-sīdantu*; *gha-sadantu* [means] let them sit down (*āsīdantu*). 2. *kha-jha-jha-ta3-bha-śa-devānupa*; *ta1-2-devānurūpa* [means] conforming to the gods (*devānurūpa*).
3. *kha-ta3-na-bha-jānan*; *jha-janmāni*; *jha-śa janān*; *ta1-2-janānām*.
O Agni, being kindled, come hither toward us; come together on one chariot with Indra and the swift gods.
May Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacred grass.
"Vāṭ! Svāhā! May all the gods, being immortal, rejoice! Thus [it is said].
The third hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with “agni vo devam,” is the seerly composition of Vasiṣṭha; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and addressed to Agni.
Regarding its address to Agni, the Anukramaṇikā states: “agni vo daśa.
These ten hymns beginning with “agni vo devam”—excluding the third and fourth—are employed in the Prātaranuvāka during the Āgneya sacrifice, in the Triṣṭubh meter, and in the Āśvina Śastra.

And it is stated in the Sūtra: “In the case of the ten [days] of the *vyūha-daśarātra*, one should extract the third and fourth [verses] from the hymn beginning with ‘agni vo devam’” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 4.13).
In the eighth day of the *vyūha-daśarātra*, this hymn serves as the *ājya-śastra*. For it is prescribed: “On the second [day], the *ājya* [śastra] is ‘agni vo devam’” (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 8.10).
O mortals, with your fires, make Agni—the god who is in harmony with the fires, the most excellent sacrificer, the messenger at the rite—your envoy;
he who is steadfast among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, whose head is flame, whose food is ghee, the purifier.

In harmony with the fires, make Agni your god—the most excellent sacrificer, the messenger at the rite—him who is steadfast among mortals, the possessor of truth, whose head is flame, who feeds on ghee, the purifier. 1.

O gods, you [should] make him—the shining one, Agni, who is united with other fires—your messenger in the sacrifice free from crookedness; [make him] most worthy of worship, [united] with those who are in harmony. (The nominative is used in the sense of the accusative. Make Agni the messenger in the *adhvara*, the sacrifice devoid of deceit.

That Agni, who, though being a god, is firmly established among mortals; who is *ṛtāvā*—possessing the sacrifice or possessing truth; whose head is heat and splendor; who has clarified butter as his food; and who is the purifier.
Like a horse with a forelock eager for pasture, he has stepped forth from the great enclosure;
the wind blows after his flame, and your path is black.
He rushes forward like a horse eager for pasture, when he has stepped forth from the great assembly. Then the wind blows after his flame; indeed, your path becomes black.

When the fire, like a horse eager for fodder, eating and snorting—that is, making a sound as it moves—emerges from its great enclosure or confinement in the form of a forest fire and spreads across the dense trees, then the wind blows following the flame of that fire.
Now follows the direct praise:
immediately thereafter, O Agni, your path (*vrajana*) is black;
the particle *sma* is used as a filler.
When you, the newly born bull Agni, have been kindled, those ageless ones move about as they tend you;
your ruddy smoke rises toward the oblation, for as a messenger, O Agni, you go to the gods.
O Agni, for you, the bull newly born, these ageless kindling-sticks blaze; your ruddy smoke rises toward the heated milk-vessel, for as a messenger, O Agni, you go forth to the gods. 3.

1. Being kindled (*samidhyamānaḥ*): O Agni, of you who are newly born (*navajātasya*), the showerer (*vṛṣṇaḥ*), whose undecaying (*ajarāḥ*) flames, being kindled (*idhānāḥ*), rise up and go forth; his smoke, ascending (*āruhaḥ*), goes toward its place, toward heaven.
O Agni, being the messenger (*dūtaḥ*), you indeed go to the gods and you gather them together.

When your power spread across the earth, when you gathered food for the people with your strides, you went forth like a released army; like one who seeks grain, you entered the offering with your tongue.
O Viṣṇu, your power has reached across the earth; when you have gathered together the foods for the one who offers, it is like an unleashed army, like a spreading net.
(Ṛgveda 5.87.4)
O Agni, shine forth or bestow upon us these visible blessings— these beautiful riches— and furthermore,
may we obtain a son who is wise, endowed with excellent intelligence, and the performer of the rites of sacrifice.
This is the form resulting from the addition of another phoneme to the root *van*, which has the meaning "to obtain" (*saṃbhana*).
May all things, every kind of wealth, belong to the praisers, the chanters, and those who sing and recite [your praises].
May you and all your retinue always, at all times, protect and guard us with blessings and well-being.
The fourth hymn, consisting of ten verses beginning with "pra vaḥ śukrāya," is the seerly composition of Vasiṣṭha; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and is addressed to Agni.
It is introduced by the words "pra vaḥ.
Its ritual application (viniyoga) is stated as being the second among the ten hymns in the Prātaranuvāka and the Niśastra.
In the animal sacrifice dedicated to Agni among the eleven [animals], the verse "pra vaḥ śukrāya" is the offering prayer (*yājyā*) for the omentum (*vapā*).
And it is stated in the Sūtra: "pra vaḥ śukrāya bhānave bharadhvam yathā viprasya manuṣo havirbhiḥ" (Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra 3.7).
Bring forth an offering and a well-purified hymn for your bright radiance, for Agni,
who moves by his knowledge between all divine and human generations.
Bring forth the oblation and the well-purified prayer for Agni, for his bright radiance—Agni who, with wisdom, moves between all divine and human generations.
O you who are the bearers of oblations, bring forth for the bright, radiant, and blazing Agni a well-purified offering and a prayer of praise.
That Agni who, by means of his wisdom (*vidmanā*)— that is, by his knowledge or path— goes (*jigāti*) between all divine and human races (*mānuṣā janūṃṣi*),
meaning he proceeds to carry the oblations between the gods and men.
May that Agni be skillful even as he is young, from whom, the youngest, he was born of his mother;
he who, bright-toothed, embraces the forests, and consumes even abundant food at once with his kindled fuel.
He is the wise Agni, though he is but young; for from his mother he was born as the youngest. He who, with pure teeth, gathers the forests together, devours even abundant food at once.
He alone is indeed *vṛtsa*, the wise;
thus Yāska says: “*Vṛtsa* is a name for the wise” (*Nirukta* 9.5).
*Agni* is *taruṇaḥ*, the one who brings across.
Then, when he was born from the mother forest as the youngest and most youthful one—
that Agni, radiant and shining, who by his own nature unites and joins together every forest tree— then [he shines].
Furthermore, he immediately—indeed, at once—completely devours even his own abundant foods.
In the assembly of this god, in his presence, the mortals have seized him who is bright white;
he who has rejected the human snare has withered the one who is difficult to dwell with for the sake of the living man.
In the encounter of this god, whom mortals have seized—the white one—who has uttered his defiance against the human snare; he has withered the dwelling-place for the mortal who acts like a foe. 3.

1. [The syllables] *kha*, *jha*, *ma* are pure (*śuddha*). 2. *kha*, *jha*, *ta*, *na*, *bha*, *ya*, *śa* are the various arrangements (*vidhāni*). 3. *kha* means "it bears" (*bibhrati*) and also "the earth becomes" (*bhūmiśca bhavati*); *gha* means "let it be" (*astu bhavati*). 4. *kha*, *bha* mean "it kindles" (*samidati*); *na*, *śa* mean "it bestows" (*samadāti*). In the presence (*anīke*), in the assembly (*saṃsadi*), in the place (*sthāne*) of this god Agni, men (*martāsaḥ*) have grasped (*jagṛbhe*) and taken hold of that white, radiant (*śubhra*) Agni. And that Agni has spoken forth (*ni uvoca*) the praise (*gubhaṃ*) performed by men (*pauruṣeyīṃ*).
In this context, the word *vaciḥ* functions in the sense of service.
The meaning is "he should serve.
That *agni* [is for] *āyave*, for the sake of humans;
for *āyavaḥ* is listed among the names of humans in the glossary as "the invokers (*hūhavaḥ*) are the *āyavaḥ*."
It shines, blazing in such a way that it is difficult to look upon and hard to endure for others.
This seer Viṣṇu Pracetas, the immortal Agni, has been established among mortals.
O mighty one, do not lead us astray here; may we always be well-disposed toward you.
This Agni, the seer among seers, the wise one among mortals, has been established as the immortal. May he not abandon us here;
may we, though being formless like waters, not sit around in exclusion.
And thus Yāska says: "The word *apsas* is a name for form" (Nirukta 5.13).
And may we not sit around those who are devoid of service (*adruvas*).
May I be a sharer in the wealth of the gift, a possessor of eternal riches.
O Agni, let there be no remnant for me of that which is born of another; do not cut me off from the path of the one who is mindful.

For it is indeed to be approached as the wealth of the stranger; may we be masters of our own eternal riches. O Agni, there is no offspring of another for us who are left behind; do not cut off the paths of the one who lacks wisdom. 7.
For the wealth of one who is unassailable and free from debt is indeed sufficient for the assembly;
therefore, may we be masters of eternal wealth that need not be returned.
Or alternatively:
May he come; may he attain it perfectly.
Moreover, may the thousandfold charioteer, who is worthy of desire and desirable, come toward us.

O Agni, shine forth these blessings upon us; may we attain a wise and noble resolve. May all things be favorable for our worshippers and for the singer. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings. 10. O Agni, illuminate these auspicious fortunes for us. May we obtain a mind endowed with excellent wisdom. May all [blessings] belong to those who praise and to the singer. Do you all protect us always with your well-being. 10.
This Ṛg verse has been explained.
The fifth hymn, consisting of nine verses beginning with “prāgnaye tavase,” is the seerly composition (ārṣa) of Vasiṣṭha; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and has Vaiśvānara as its deity.
Thus it is enumerated: “prāgnaye nava vaiśvānarīya tu. The application (viniyoga) is indicated by the mark (laiṅgika).

Bring forth a song of praise to the mighty Agni, the messenger of heaven and earth; he who, as Vaiśvānara, has grown strong in the lap of all the immortals through those who are ever watchful. 1. Bring forth a song of praise to the mighty Agni, the messenger of heaven and earth; he who, as Vaiśvānara, has grown strong in the lap of all the immortals through those who are ever watchful.
O singers, bring forth your song of praise to the powerful, exalted Agni Vaiśvānara—the guest of heaven, the mid-air, and the earth—who goes as a messenger;

that Vaiśvānara Agni, who is dear to all men, who dwells in the lap of all the immortal gods at the sacrifice, and who, being accompanied by the ever-watchful gods, grows great through hymns and oblations.

Agni has been established as the back of heaven and upon the earth; he is the leader of the rivers, the bull of the stars. As Vaiśvānara, increasing by his choice, he shines forth toward the human tribes. pṛṣṭhaḥ | in heaven | has been placed | Agni | upon the earth | the leader | of the rivers | the bull | of the stars | he | toward the human | tribes | shines forth | Vaiśvānara | increasing | by his choice || 2 ||

The leader of the Sindhus, the rivers, and the stiryās— waters which, according to the statement of Yāska, "become stiryās because they flow" (Nirukta 6.17)— he who is the bull, the showerer, the one praised on the back, or the one joined with splendor, that Agni who has been established in heaven, in the intermediate space, and on earth; he, Vaiśvānara, the fire belonging to all men, increasing through the most excellent oblation or through splendor, shines forth toward the human tribes, toward human progeny.

Out of fear of you, O Vaiśvānara, the Asikrī tribes fled, abandoning their food and possessions, as you, O Agni, blazing forth, shone brightly while destroying the ancient fortresses. 3. Out of fear of you, the tribes went away—the Asikrīs, who were not [even] swimming, abandoning their enjoyments. O Vaiśvānara, when you, shining intensely, O Agni, did shine while driving away the ancient fortresses. 3.
1. From the *kha-ya-śas-tiryāna* [meter]; not from the *tiryāna*.
O Vaiśvānara, Agni who is devoid of all men (*viśvanarahita*), out of fear (*bhiyā*) of you, the dark-colored (*asiknīḥ*) royal [waters] have flowed.
In the first noble [truth], the second [is applied].
The subjects—the people, being of discordant minds yet gathered together—came, arriving while abandoning and forsaking their enjoyments and riches.
When? He says:
when, glowing and shining brightly for the sake of the former king, you blazed forth, rending the fortresses of his enemies.
And thus says the Nigama: "O King, I am the one who first bestowed wealth" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1.63.7).
The entire threefold world, both earth and heaven, O Vaiśvānara, follow your command from the beginning.
You have overspread the two worlds with your light, blazing with unceasing radiance.
The three worlds—the earth and the sky—O Vaiśvānara Agni, follow thy ordinance. With thy light thou hast overspread the two worlds, shining with thy unceasing flame. 4.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, leader of all men,
thus generating abundant light for the person performing ritual action, you have driven the dasyus— those devoid of ritual action and seekers of enjoyment— from their place by means of strength.

Being born in the highest heaven, you instantly protect the path like Vāyu. Bringing forth the worlds, O Jātavedas, you have roared aloud, bestowing gifts upon the noble man. 7. Being born; in the highest; heaven; like Vāyu; the path; around; you protect; instantly; you; the worlds; generating; you have roared; for the noble man; O Jātavedas; bestowing. 7.

O Vaiśvānara, you who are well-known, being born in the highest, most distant firmament— the intermediate space— manifesting in the form of the sun, you drink the *pātha* (the Soma) immediately, just as Vāyu drinks the Soma first among the dual-deity cups;
or rather, like Vāyu, you protect— that is, you drink around— the *pātha*, the water.
The meaning is "you dry up. Furthermore, O Jātavedas—O Agni whose nature is born—you [dry up] the *bhuvanāni*, that is, the waters;
for the word *bhuvana* is listed among the names for water in the lexicon.
Generating offspring for the sake of protecting the progeny for the sacrificer, bestowing desires, you indeed roar toward [us] with your Vaiśvānara self; you thunder or you bellow.

O Agni Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas, send forth that nourishing food to us, full of splendor; so that you may swell our wealth, O possessor of all boons, and grant wide renown to the mortal who offers oblations. 8. That [food], O Agni, for us—send it forth, O Vaiśvānara, full of light, O Jātavedas; so that you may cause prosperity to flow, O possessor of all boons, and bestow wide fame upon the mortal who gives. 8.
O Jātavedas, whose wisdom is born; O Vaiśvānara, benefactor of all; O Agni, send forth toward us that nourishment which is desirable, that rain which is full of light.
For by means of rain, the three worlds indeed shine—or rather: [the verse continues].
"Bestow that shining nourishment upon Agni.
And thus it is heard in scripture: "Therefore, he for whom there is most food, he alone shines most brightly in the world" (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 1.5).
Alternatively, bestow that desirable, shining, and radiant nourishment.
Just as you cause the rain-stalk to swell with wealth and protect it, so too,
O Viśvavāra— O Agni who possesses all desirable things— you cause broad and extensive fame to swell for the mortal sacrificer who offers oblations.

O Agni Vaiśvānara, bestow upon us and our patrons that wealth which abounds in food, and grant us renowned strength; together with the Rudras and the Vasus, being well-pleased, O Agni, extend great protection to us. 9. [That] for us, O Agni, [bestow] upon the patrons, [that] wealth rich in cattle, [and] bestow [upon us] renown-winning strength. O Vaiśvānara, grant us great protection, O Agni, being in harmony with the Rudras and the Vasus. 9.

O Agni, for us—for those who are generous (*maghavadbhyas*), that is, for those who possess wealth and offer oblations—bestow (*ni yuvasva*) that well-known *rayi* (wealth), which is rich in food (*purukṣum*) or possesses great fame; and bestow *vāja*, which is to be heard of (*śrutyam*), as well as strength (*vājam*). Mix these together thoroughly for us.
1. śa-karmakṛte | 2. kha-dvaidatyagraheṣu; ta-dvaidatyagṛheṣu; na-dvaidatya: graheṣu | 3. kha-jha-na-bha-ya-śa-janāya | 4. kha-bha-pinvasi pālayasi.
Furthermore, O Vaiśvānara—O Agni who belongs to all men—you, being in harmony with the Rudras and the Vasus, the gods, grant us great protection and happiness.
The sixth hymn, consisting of seven verses beginning with *pra samnājaḥ*, has Vasiṣṭha as its seer.
It is enumerated thus: *pra samnājaḥ sapta*.
Since it is stated that "it belongs to Vaiśvānara," Agni Vaiśvānara is also the deity of this hymn.
The application is inferential.
I praise the glorious deeds of the Asura, the man who brings joy to the people;
like those of Indra, I laud his mighty exploits, and praising him, I speak of Dāru.
I praise the glorious deeds of the sovereign Asura, the one who brings joy to the people; like those of Indra, the mighty, I, praising him, proclaim his acts as I celebrate the wood. 1.
I bow to the breaker of the wooden fortress;
bowing, [I praise] the son of Samnaja, the lord of the entire world, the wealthy, the powerful man—
by "pauṃsya" is meant heroic vigor.
And thus Yāska says: "A man (*pumān*) is so called because he has a great mind (*purumanas*), or from the root *puṃs*.

I proclaim—the praises and the deeds performed by that Vaiśvānara, who is like Indra, the one who possesses the power of the people (*kṛṣṭīnām*), the one who is to be praised, and the one who is mighty (*tavasaḥ*). I declare his glory and his works.

They urge on the poet, the banner, the sustainer, the light from the mountain; they promote the auspicious sovereignty over heaven and earth. With songs, I celebrate the ancient, great ordinances of Agni, the breaker of forts.

They urge on the Seer, the Banner, the Support, the Radiance from the mountain; they promote his auspicious sovereignty over heaven and earth. With hymns, I seek to win through the ancient, mighty ordinances of Agni, the Fort-destroyer.

They—either the gods or my [prayers]—strengthen, please, or impel Agni Vaiśvānara, the king of sovereignty: him who is the wise poet (*kavi*), the banner (*ketu*) of the universe, the enlightener; the light (*dhāsi*) of the supporter (*dhar*), the illuminator of the singer (*ādartṛ*); the radiance (*bhānu*) that shines, the bringer of bliss (*śam*) to both heaven and earth (*rodasyoḥ*). (Note: *ādartṛ* is interpreted as "singer" based on the context of the hymn; alternatively, it may refer to one who "upholds" or "supports.")
And I, with my songs, celebrate—the ancient, great, and eternal deeds and vows of Indra, the shatterer of forts and the lord of the thunderbolt. I serve him with my hymns.
Agni has driven away those who are knotted with deceit, whose speech is harsh, who are impure, faithless, ignorant, and devoid of sacrifice;
he, the foremost, has cast down those Dasyus and made the non-sacrificers subject to others.

Agni has driven far away those Dasyus who perform no rites, who are knotted with deceit, whose speech is hostile, who are impure, faithless, ignorant, and devoid of sacrifice; he, the foremost, has made those who do not worship his own subjects.

Agni has utterly driven away those who perform no sacrifices, who are hypocritical, who are mere talkers, whose speech is wicked, whose words are harmful, who are traders (the Paṇis), usurers, lacking faith in sacrifices, who exalt themselves with praises, who are devoid of sacrifice— those thieves who spend their time in vain. Agni, being the foremost and preeminent, has made them inferior and lowly, those who do not offer sacrifices.
1. According to Jña, it is the Ṛṣi's [verse] in the Triṣṭubh meter. 2. According to Ya and Sasa, [it is as follows].
3. According to Kha and Bha, it is "masculinity"; according to Jña, Ta, and Na, it is "manliness"; according to Śa, it is "the state of Pūṣan."

4. [The letters] kha, jha, na, bha, and śa represent Agni... the letter ca is not present; preceded by gha, the ancient Agni made other men who were non-sacrificers fit for sacrifice; preceded by ta, the most excellent leader Agni... "made"—the meaning is "he makes."

I praise that Agni, the lord of wealth, who, the most heroic leader, by his powers turned those rejoicing [beings] who were in the western darkness toward the east; him who is never bowed down, who subdues those who attack us. He, the most heroic leader, Agni, by his powers—the wisdom bestowed upon them—turned those beings who were immersed in the western, unilluminated darkness, while they were rejoicing and praising, toward the east, moving straight forward. Or rather: he, the most heroic leader, Agni, by his powers—his insights—turned the night-rejoicing dawns toward the east. I praise that Agni, the lord of wealth, who is unbowed, who subdues those who desire battle.

He who, with his weapons, brought low the embodied ones; he who made the Dawns have the Sun as their lord—Agni, the mighty one, having subdued the tribes of Nahuṣa by his powers, made them payers of tribute. He who, with his weapons (vadhrasraiḥ), brought down the embodied (dehyaḥ)—the fortified Asuraic sciences—and made the Dawns have the Sun (arya) as their husband; that great (yahvaḥ) Agni, having subdued the people (viśaḥ) by his powers (sahobhiḥ), made the tribes of Nahuṣa (nahuṣaḥ) givers of tribute (balihṛtaḥ). *Note on terminology:* * *Dehyaḥ*: "embodied," referring here to the personified or fortified demonic forces. * *Vadhrasraiḥ*: "with weapons" or "with slaying tools. * *Aryapatnīḥ*: "having the noble one (the Sun) as their husband. * *Nahuṣaḥ*: A specific royal lineage or a class of beings associated with it. * *Bali-hṛtaḥ*: "tribute-payers" or "those who bring offerings. * *Sahobhiḥ*: "by his powers" or "by his strengths."*

In whose protection all people have stood with their movements, seeking his benevolence—Vaiśvānara Agni, the most excellent, has taken his seat in the lap of the two parents, Heaven and Earth. In whose protection all people have stood with their movements, seeking his benevolence—Vaiśvānara Agni, the most excellent, has taken his seat in the lap of the two parents, Heaven and Earth. All people, for the sake of happiness (*śarman*), standing near Vaiśvānara while praying for his benevolence (*sumati*) through their movements (*evaiḥ*)—that is, through their ritual acts or oblations—stand near him; he whom they thus approach, that Vaiśvānara, Agni, being the Sun, has taken his seat in the most excellent lap (*upastha*) of the two parents, Heaven and Earth—that is, in the intermediate space of the atmosphere.

The god Vaiśvānara has taken up the treasures from the depths at the rising of the sun; from the lower ocean and from the higher, from heaven and from earth, Agni has taken them up with these [rays]. 1. *kha*: in darkness that is not shining; 2. *kha-na-bha*: he praises; 3. *kha*: accumulated by bodies.
Vaiśvānara is Agni who belongs to all men; he is the shining deity. By his intelligence, he perceives the intermediate spaces (*antarikṣa*). *Bubha* refers to the intermediate space;
thus Yāska says: "The intermediate space is *bubha*, or else it is so called because waters rich in ghee (*ghṛta*) are bound within it" (Nirukta 10.44).
The *vasūni* are the darknesses that cover;
the root is *vasa ācchādane* (to cover). When the sun has risen—upon its rising—I take them away.
From the ocean, from the intermediate space—
since "Sagara is the ocean" is read among the names for the intermediate space—
from the lower earth, I have seized the darknesses.
From the ocean beyond, and even from heaven, he has taken away the darknesses.
He demonstrates this very point:
Agni has taken away the darknesses from heaven, and he has taken away the darknesses from the earth as well.
The seventh hymn, consisting of seven verses beginning with “pra vo devam,” is the seerly composition of Vasiṣṭha; it is in the Triṣṭubh meter and is addressed to Agni.
This is indicated by the introductory formula: “pra vo devam.”
The application of the ten hymns for the Prātaranuvāka and the Ādhina-śastra has been stated.
I impel with salutations the god who is swift of thought, like a prize-winning steed;
may he, the wise one, become our messenger at the sacrifice, for he, moving with measured pace, has found his place among the gods.

I send forth for you the god Agni, the victorious one, like a spirited horse, with acts of homage. As the wise messenger of our sacrifice, he has found his place among the gods by himself, moving with measured pace.

O Agni, you who are a god endowed with qualities such as brilliance, the subduer of Rākṣasas, or one who exerts power; O Agni, the leader of the foremost, like a horse—swift, impetuous, or powerful—I send you forth with salutations or hymns of praise. O Agni, I indeed send you forth.
Furthermore, O Agni, being wise and knowing, become the messenger of our sacrifice (adhvara).
Now follows a praise in the third person.

By himself, by his own self, he is known among the gods like Agni, the swift-moving burner. Come, O Agni, along the broad earth; you who are delightful, enjoying the noble gift of the gods. Resounding with your might upon the ridges of the earth, burn down all the forests with your jaws.

Come hither, O Agni, along the broad earth, according to your own will—joyful, enjoying the excellent offering of the gods—making the ridges of the earth resound with your vigor, burning all the forests at your pleasure with your jaws.

O Agni, you who are *mandra*—the one who gladdens or the one worthy of praise—[enjoying] the friendship of the gods, that is to say, friendship with the gods; *juṣāṇaḥ*, meaning serving or enjoying; [you who] make resound—that is, cause to sound—the elevated surface of the earth, such as grass, shrubs, and so forth, with *śuṣmaiḥ*, that is, with drying, burning, and scorching splendors.
For that which is being burned makes a sound;
"with jaws" means with fangs—
that is to say, with flames.
O you who burn with desire, burning all the woods,
come hither, come hither, along your own paths— that is, by your own ways.
The repetition of the form is for the sake of emphasis:
"The ancient sacrifice is well-prepared, for the sacrificial grass is strewn; Agni, being praised, is the gratified Hotṛ-priest.
Calling upon the two Mothers who possess all boons, from whom, O most youthful one, you were born as the gracious one."

The ancient sacrifice is well-prepared; for Agni, being praised like a Hotṛ priest, takes pleasure in it. Invoking the two Mothers who possess all boons, O Most Youthful One, from whom you were born as one most gracious. ||3||

1. In *kha* and *bha*, [the word] is *uditau sūrye*. 2. In *ta*, *rdaśasūkteṣu*. 3. In *kha*, *jha*, *ta*, and *śa*, [it is] *tvām*; in *na* and *bha*, *tvam*. 4. In *kha*, *jha*, and *śa*, *tvam*. 5. In *kha* and *bha*, *prahiṇomyeva*. 6. In *jha* and *tara*, *ya-devān jānan*. 7. In *ta*, *sevamānaḥ san*. This sacrifice (*yajñaḥ*) is "eastward" (*prācīnaḥ*); the meaning is that it is performed correctly.
Or alternatively:
the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the Hotṛ priest are oriented toward the east.
Or alternatively:

The sacrifice is the oblation; it is directed forward, being fastened facing the east. For the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) is well-placed and firmly established upon the grass. Agni, being praised and lauded, is gratified and becomes satisfied.
He is both the *hotṛ* priest and not the *hotṛ*.
The word "not" (*na*) has the sense of "and.
Invoking the two Mothers, Heaven and Earth—who are all-encompassing (*viśvavāre*, meaning "possessing all desirable things")—he becomes present within the *iḍā* offering.
To the question "When?", he says: O *yaviṣṭha*, most youthful one, when you are born—that is, when you arise—as *suśeva*, very gracious and full of happiness.
Immediately at the sacrifice, the discerning men brought forth the charioteer who belongs to them;
Agni has been established in the house as the lord of the people—the delightful one, sweet of speech, and true to the Eternal Law.

Immediately at the sacrifice, the discerning men brought forth the charioteer; he who has been established as the lord of these people in the dwelling—Agni, the delightful, the sweet-voiced, the observer of Truth. 4.
The wise ones, those of discerning insight—human beings—at the sacrifice, the ritual, immediately generate Agni, the charioteer, the possessor of the chariot, the leader.

He who carries their oblation is this Agni, the lord of the people (*viśapati*), the lord of all, or the joyful one, the exhilarator, the one whose speech is sweet, the one whose words are intoxicating, the observer of truth, the possessor of sacrifice; he has been established, placed within the dwelling, the house of the people, of men.
The chosen Vahni has ascended; Brahmā, the distributor, has come to the assembly of men.
Both Heaven and Earth have magnified him whom the Hotṛ priest worships as the possessor of all boons.

He has been mounted; he is encompassed; he is the bearer of oblations; having arrived, Agni is the priest in the assembly of men, the distributor of wealth—he whom both Heaven and Earth have magnified, whom the Hotṛ-priest worships as the possessor of all boons. ||5||

Chosen for the office of Hotṛ, the carrier who conveys the oblations, the Brahman, the sovereign, the sustainer and supporter of all—Agni, having come from the heavenly world or being of the nature of one who arrives, has sat down in the assembly of men, in the station of the Hotṛ.
That Agni whom both Heaven and Earth cause to grow and increase.
And he whom the human Hotṛ priest worships, he who possesses all boons and is desirable by all.

These men have surpassed all things in glory—they who, being heroic, have fashioned the prayer as their choice; they who, listening, have furthered the people; and those who have come to me with this long-lasting truth.

These [gods], through their splendors, have surpassed every prayer—those heroic ones who have fashioned the choice [hymn], who, listening, have extended the people, and who [have accepted] this long-lasting truth of mine. 6.

These men of mine, through their glorious fires (*dyumnair agnibhiḥ*), surpass—that is, they cause to increase—the entire world of living beings (*viśvaṃ pūvyavargam*). Alternatively, through their glorious oblations (*dyumnair havirbhiḥ*), they surpass—that is, they reach—the entire world. This is the meaning.

To the question "Who?", he says: those who are *vīryāḥ*, i.e., humans (*manuṣyāḥ*), have *vatakṣan*, i.e., fashioned (*samastakurvan*)— the particle *vā* being used as a conjunction (*samuccaye*)— the *mantram*, i.e., the hymn (*stotram*), or the object of praise (*stutyam*), which is *varam*, i.e., sufficient (*paryāptam*).
And those people of the clans who are listening.
Regarding the root *śru*, there is reduplication by the rule "asanyoḥ" [Pāṇini 6.1.9], and the suffix *san* is treated as having a *jhal* sound by the rule "iko jhal" [Pāṇini 1.2.9].
Furthermore, all grammatical operations—[1.
kha-°māsañjam; jña-ta-na-bha-śa-°māsanam | 2. kha-ma- 'rathiraṃ' is not present | 3. kha. madayitṛ° | 4. ta-ṛtavā | 5. jha-°dātiranta ābharanta | 6. ya-aramalam]—[apply].

The forms do not occur because [the rule] "in the Veda they are optional" applies; rather, the middle voice (ātmanepada) occurs by the rule "after the roots jñā, śru, smṛ, and dṛś, when followed by saN. They "extend," that is, they increase. "My"—meaning mine—or "those who" [increase] this "truth" (ṛta), namely this fire; here the genitive case is used in the sense of the object (karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī), as in the expression "he approached the women" (māpāṇām abhyaiyat). "They have caused to shine," that is, they have made it shine.
Now we, the Vasiṣṭhas, implore you, O Agni, Son of Strength, the lord of riches;
grant this to our patrons who praise you. Protect us always with your blessings.
Now we Vasiṣṭhas entreat you, O Agni, the lord of riches, O Son of Strength; may this [prayer] reach the patrons who praise you. Do you all protect us always with blessings. 7.
By what well-fashioned hymn, O Agni, will you distinguish us? When, being praised, will you grant us our own inherent power?
O bounteous giver, when shall we become masters and winners of wealth that is difficult to overcome and truly excellent?

By what [means], O Agni, do you not reject our well-fashioned hymn? What desire or self-dependent power will you grant when you are praised? When, O bounteous giver, shall we become masters of wealth and winners of that which is difficult to overcome and excellent? 3.

O Agni, by what inherent power (*svadhā*) do you illuminate, pervade, or clothe our well-fashioned hymn of praise (*suvṛkti*) with the oblation? And what specific power, being praised and extolled, will you attain?
O Agni, bestower of beautiful gifts (*sudatra*).
And thus Yāska says: "Sudatra means one who gives auspicious gifts" (Nirukta 6.14).
When shall we become masters—that is, lords—of *rāyaḥ*, wealth that is *sādhuḥ*, excellent, yet difficult for enemies to overcome and destructive to them?
And when shall we become givers—that is, sharers [of wealth]?

I hear of the devotion of Bharata’s son; when he shines forth greatly like the sun, the domestic one (*damūnāḥ*)—whether interpreted as *dāntamanāḥ* (one whose mind is subdued), *damamanāḥ* (one whose mind is tamed), or *dānamanāḥ* (one whose mind is generous)—is seen dispelling the darkness of the nights that bring rest, or the darkness of the people, the subjects, or the sacrificers.
Or alternatively: [the text continues...]
He dispels the darkness; this is the meaning of "he causes it to vanish.
Unerring, a seer, Aditi, Vivasvat, a good comrade, Mitra, and a gracious guest—he of wondrous rays shines at the forefront of the dawns, the embryo of the waters, the sprout of plants.
He entered.

Unerring, a seer, unbound, radiant, a good companion, a friend, a guest, auspicious to us—Agni, with his wondrous luster, shines forth like the dawn; the germ of the waters, he has entered the plants. 3.

That Agni who is *amūra*—unerring and undeluded; *kavi*—wise and insightful; *aditi*—inexhaustible and noble; *vivasvān*—resplendent; *susaṃsat*—possessing a beautiful seat or excellent consciousness; *mitra*—a friend and protector of all; *atithi*—worthy of worship like a guest; *śiva*—the bringer of auspiciousness to the world; and *citrabhānu*—of variegated radiance.

O Agni, Vasiṣṭha, kindling thee, shall slay Jarūtha; grant us abundant wisdom for the sake of wealth. O Jātavedas, praise [the gods] with many hymns! And you all, protect us evermore with blessings. (6) O Agni, the seer Vasiṣṭha, kindling thee, becomes thy priest. And thou, slay Jarūtha—the host of Rākṣasas who speak harshly or are subject to decay. For the sake of the wealthy sacrificer, grant *purandhi*—abundant wisdom or the host of gods; as Yāska says: "Purandhi is one of many thoughts. Sacrifice (*yakṣi*). Furthermore, O Jātavedas Agni, with many hymns (*puruṇīthā*), praise the gods. Or rather, cause the destruction of the many-holed dwellings of the Rākṣasas. The fifteenth hymn, beginning with "Upo na jāraḥ," consists of fifteen verses; it is the Ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha’s composition, in the Triṣṭubh meter, addressed to Agni. Thus it is recorded: "Upo na jāra. Its application is prescribed for the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina Śastra.

Like the lover of the Dawn, he has assumed his broad radiance; flashing and shining brightly, he blazes forth. The pure, golden bull shines with his light; impelling our prayers, he has awakened those who desire him. Like the lover of the Dawn, he has assumed his broad radiance; flashing and shining brightly, he blazes forth. The pure, golden bull shines with his light; impelling our prayers, he has awakened those who desire him. Agni, like the lover of the Dawn—that is, like the Sun who is the lover of the Dawn—has taken to himself his *pṛthu pājaḥ*, his wide-extending brilliance. Furthermore, although the words *davidyutat*, *dīdyat*, and *śośucānaḥ* all denote the act of shining, they are employed here to indicate the intensity of that light; thus there is no tautology. The meaning is "shining exceedingly. He is the *vṛṣā*, the showerer of desires; the *hariḥ*, the impeller of oblations; the *śuciḥ*, the purifier Agni. *Hinvānaḥ*, impelling our *dhiyaḥ*, our ritual acts, he *ā bhāti*, shines forth with his *bhāsā*, his splendor. Moreover, *uśatīḥ*, those who long for him, he *ajīgaḥ*, he awakens; he brings forth the creatures who were hidden by darkness.

Like the sun at the breaking of dawn, he has shone before the mornings; like the Uśij priests extending the sacrifice with their thought, Agni, the god who knows all births, hastens hither as the messenger, going to the gods, the most bountiful. At the breaking of day (*vastauḥ*), like the sun (*svaḥ*) at the approach of the dawns, he has shone (*aroci*). Like the Uśij priests (*uśijaḥ*) performing the sacrifice (*yajñam tanvānāḥ*) with their hymns of praise (*manma*), so too does Agni. And furthermore, the knowing one (*vidvān*), the messenger (*dūtaḥ*) of the gods, traveling toward the gods (*devayāvā*), the most generous giver (*vaniṣṭhaḥ*), Agni hastens forth in various ways (*vi ā dravat*).
1. Kha-bha-vasiṣṭha is the seer (ṛṣi).
2. Ya-ādhayati [is the deity]. 3. Jha-deva is the blazing fire, knowing the births—that is, the origins—of all beings.

Toward him [Agni], our thoughts, seeking the gods and begging for wealth, go forth with songs of praise—toward him who is fair to behold, of beautiful countenance, possessed of noble steeds, the bearer of oblations, the protector of men. The hymns, which are in the form of praises, desiring the gods and begging for riches, approach Agni with their voices—him who is lovely to look upon, of beautiful appearance, with excellent horses, the carrier of sacrificial offerings, and the refuge of human beings.

O Agni, being well-pleased with the Vasus, bring Indra to us; being united with the Rudras, bring the mighty Rudra; being joined with the Ādityas, bring Aditi who is beneficial to all people; and being accompanied by the Ṛks—the Aṅgirases—bring Bṛhaspati, the bestower of all boons. Indra | us | O Agni | with the Vasus | well-pleased | Rudra | with the Rudras | hither | bring | the mighty one | with the Ādityas | Aditi | beneficial to all people | Bṛhaspati | with the Ṛks | the possessor of all boons || 4 || O Agni, you who are in harmony with the Vasu deities, bring Indra for our sake; being united with the Rudra deities, bring the great Rudra; being joined with the Āditya deities, bring Aditi who is for the welfare of all mankind; and being accompanied by the Ṛks—the praising Aṅgirases—bring Bṛhaspati, who is honored by all.

The eager clans praise Agni—the delightful Hotṛ, the youngest—at the sacrifices; for he has become the protector of riches through the night, the unwearied messenger for the gods at the sacrifice. The eager clans—the humans—praise Agni at the sacrifices: the delightful one who is to be lauded, the invoker, the youngest, the most youthful. For that reason, he has become the protector of riches (*kṣapāvān*) during the night—for indeed, the Agnihotra is offered at night—and the unwearied messenger for the gods at the sacrifice for the sake of the sacrificers who possess wealth and oblations. Thus it is heard in the Śruti: "Because he became the messenger, therefore they praise him with joined hands at the sacrifice. 13. Mandram | hotāram | uśijaḥ | yaviṣṭham | agnim | viśaḥ | īḷate | adhvareṣu | saḥ | hi | kṣapāvān | abhavat | rayīṇām | atandraḥ | dūtaḥ | yajñāya | devān || 5 || Uśijaḥ (eager), viśaḥ (clans), mandram (delightful), hotāram (invoker), yaviṣṭham (youngest), agnim (Agni), viśaḥ (clans), īḷate (they praise), adhvareṣu (at the sacrifices). Saḥ (he), hi (for), kṣapāvān (protector of the night), abhavat (became), rayīṇām (of riches), atandraḥ (unwearied), dūtaḥ (messenger), yajñāya (for the sacrifice), devān (to the gods). 5. Uśijaḥ (the eager ones), viśaḥ (the clans), mandram (the delightful one), hotāram (the invoker), yaviṣṭham (the youngest), agnim (Agni), adhvareṣu (at the sacrifices), īḷate (they praise). Hi (because), saḥ (he), kṣapāvān (the protector of the night)—for the Agnihotra is indeed offered at night—rayīṇām (of the wealthy), atandraḥ (unwearied), dūtaḥ (messenger), abhavat (became). And thus it is heard: "Because he became the messenger, therefore they praise him with joined hands at the sacrifice. 13.
